collections.title: Everyday worlds
collections.description: What did the land, houses, food, and work of ordinary life demand from people?

collections.title: Power and legitimacy
collections.description: How did rulers persuade, recruit, challenge, and sometimes lose the people around them?

collections.title: Across the water
collections.description: Explore trade routes, maritime contact, diplomacy, and the movement of ideas.

collections.title: Cities and society
collections.description: From early settlement to digital cities: communities continually remake their environments.

collections.title: Moments of change
collections.description: Follow crises, new political settlements, and the uncertain aftermath of pivotal events.

collections.title: New voices of the archive
collections.description: Newly written stories from fields, politics, households and changing workplaces.

collections.title: Fields and households
collections.description: A route through shelter, farming, obligations and changing family life.

collections.title: Learning and service
collections.description: Why societies sought educated officials, and who had the chance to become one.

collections.title: Institutions in motion
collections.description: From early commanderies to civilian democracy, trace how authority changes.

collections.title: The long history behind the headline
collections.description: Read substantial essays, inspect their reference notes, and follow why one century raises questions for another.

collections.title: Hangul: the complete Chapter
collections.description: Follow ten connected readings from Korean writing before Hangul to the earliest writing debates, books, and spelling practices.

collections.title: The Korean War: the complete Chapter
collections.description: Read ten connected subjects from the outbreak through coalition warfare, civilian survival and the armistice.

collections.title: Silla: the complete rise of a kingdom
collections.description: Ten connected histories from fourth-century uncertainty through political reform, Jinheung’s expansion, queenship and the coalition of Chunchu and Yushin.

collections.title: Liberation to Partition: the complete Chapter
collections.description: Ten linked studies follow the local awakening of 1945 through occupation, political rivalry, social crisis, and divided state formation.

collections.title: After 1945: governing and surviving
collections.description: A thematic detour from the end of empire through local political organization, everyday survival, and the outbreak of war.

collections.title: Baekje: the complete river and maritime kingdom
collections.description: Ten connected studies follow the Han basin court, international exchange, the 475 catastrophe, Ungjin recovery, Sabi culture, and the fall of 660.

collections.title: Silla: everyday lives and unequal opportunities
collections.description: Ten connected studies of households, fields, craft, trade, cities, health and leisure beyond the royal court.

collections.title: Gojoseon: archaeological evidence and historical memory
collections.description: Ten connected studies compare Bronze Age evidence, transmitted Joseon–Yan encounters, contested origin traditions and later uses of antiquity.

collections.title: Opening Korea: the full treaty-port Chapter
collections.description: Ten connected histories of commerce, jurisdiction, Qing and Japanese diplomacy, technical learning, ideas, and the 1882 United States treaty.

collections.title: Later Joseon: families and everyday life
collections.description: Ten connected studies of lineages, marriage, childhood, labor, houses, clothing, food, illness and mourning in a changing society.

collections.title: Goryeo: the full founding and consolidation Chapter
collections.description: Ten connected studies show how royal marriages, uncertain succession, reforms, land revenue, provincial administration and court memory shaped a dynasty after 936.

collections.title: Goryeo: religion and the many worlds of belief
collections.description: Ten linked histories of kingship, monastic work, learning, rites, lay devotion, and the meeting of Buddhist and Confucian practice.

collections.title: Korean independence: movements and contested strategies
collections.description: Ten linked histories of 1919 republicanism, borderland armed movements, cultural and class politics, students, and wartime resistance.

collections.title: Ideas and expression
collections.description: Foundation stories, learning, writing, reform, and cultural influence.

collections.title: The formation of Goguryeo: tradition, landscape and early institutions
collections.description: Ten source-conscious readings tracing Jumong traditions, the Yalu landscape, kingship, early expansion, household economies and the uncertain transition to fourth-century power.

collections.title: Goguryeo: crisis, expansion, government and the northern kingdom
collections.description: Ten linked histories from the fourth-century commandery transition and Gogukwon's reversals to Jangsu's capital strategy, sixth-century political change and Yeon Gaesomun's coup.
